answer: Ridge-Wharf Forge curve: each new agent identity posts a creation deposit that scales as D = k·e^(α·R), where R is the count of prior registrations sharing its sponsor/wharf node within the epoch. Legitimate operators cluster cheaply along a flat ridge; sybil floods hit the exponential wall, making N identities cost k·(e^(αN)−1)/(e^α−1). Sponsors also forge a decaying reputation bond per referral, slashed on cluster detection, so attackers pay escalating capital plus forfeited bonds.
